hints: Square to get $2x - 1 < 4 \implies x < \frac{5}{2}$, and combine with domain $x > \frac{1}{2}$.
walkthrough:
For $f$ to be decreasing, the first derivative must be strictly negative:
$$f'(x) < 0 \implies 3(2x - 1)^{1/2} - 6 < 0$$

Divide by $3$ and isolate the square root:
$$(2x - 1)^{1/2} < 2$$

Square both sides (valid since the square root is non-negative on $x > \frac{1}{2}$):
$$2x - 1 < 4 \implies 2x < 5 \implies x < \frac{5}{2}$$

Combine with the function's domain constraint $x > \frac{1}{2}$:
$$\frac{1}{2} < x < \frac{5}{2} \quad \left(\text{or } \left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{5}{2}\right)\right)$$

Integrate the derivative with respect to $x$ using the reverse chain rule:
$$f(x) = \int \left(3(2x - 1)^{1/2} - 6\right) dx = 3 \times \frac{(2x - 1)^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2} \times 2} - 6x + c = (2x - 1)^{3/2} - 6x + c$$
